NONE: B2 strange or unexpected
奇怪的，古怪的；異常的；出人意料的

before noun: C2 [ before noun ] not happening often

NONE: › (of numbers) not able to be divided exactly by two
奇數的，單數的

before noun: › [ before noun ] (of something that should be in a pair or set) separated from its pair or set
（指一對或一組事物中）單個的，單只的，不成對的

NONE: › used after a number, especially a number that can be divided by ten, to show that the exact number is not known
（尤用於可被10整除的數字後）大約，…多一點

example: Her father was an odd man.
她父親是個古怪的人。
What an odd thing to say.
這樣說太奇怪了。
The skirt and jacket looked a little odd together.
這裙子和夾克搭配看上去有點怪。
That's odd - I'm sure I put my keys in this drawer and yet they're not here.
真奇怪——我肯定把鎖匙放進這個抽屜了，可是卻不見了。
It's odd that no one's seen him.
奇怪的是沒人見過他。
It must be odd to go back to your home town after forty years away.
離開40年後回到家鄉一定感覺很奇怪。
She does the odd teaching job but nothing permanent.
她有時教教課，但並不固定。
You get the odd person who's rude to you but they're generally quite helpful.
你不巧遇到了一個對你粗魯的人，不過他們一般是相當樂於助人的。
3, 5, and 7 are all odd numbers.
3， 5， 7都是奇數。
The houses on this side of the street all have odd numbers.
街道這邊的房子都是單號的。
He's got a whole drawer full of odd socks.
他有一抽屜的單只襪子。
I'd got a few odd (= I had various) balls of wool left over.
我有幾個花色不同的、織毛衣剩下的毛線團。

NONE: › small jobs of different types, especially those that involve repairing or cleaning things
（尤指涉及修理或清洗的）雜活，零工

example: He’s been doing odd jobs this summer to earn a little extra money.
這些夏天他打了些零工來額外掙點錢。

NONE: › a man who is paid to do different types of jobs, especially in the house or garden
（尤指在房子或花園裡）做雜活兒的人，打零工者
› a person whose behaviour is unusual and strange
古怪的人，怪異的人
› someone or something that is strange and unusual
怪人；怪事；反常現象

example: Even today a man who stays at home to take care of the children is regarded as something of an oddity.
即便在今天，人們仍然認為一個大男人呆在家裡照顧小孩是件怪事。

NONE: C2 in a strange or surprising way
奇怪地，古怪地；異常地；出人意料地

example: Didn't you think she was behaving very oddly at the party yesterday?
你難道不覺得她昨天在聚會上表現得很古怪嗎？
Oddly enough (= this is strange/surprising), she didn't mention anything about the fact that she was getting married.
真奇怪，她隻字未提自己要結婚這件事。

NONE: › small pieces, usually of cloth, that have been cut from larger pieces
零頭碎片；（通常指）布頭

example: a few oddments of fabric
幾塊零頭布料

NONE: › the quality of being strange or unexpected
奇怪；意料之外
C1 the probability (= how likely it is) that a particular thing will or will not happen
可能性，機會；幾率，概率
› in gambling (= the activity of risking money guessing the result of something), a probability expressed as a number
投注賠率

example: If you drive a car all your life, the odds are that you'll have an accident at some point.
如果你一輩子開車的話，你有可能在某一時刻發生車禍。
There are heavy odds against people succeeding in such a bad economic climate.
在如此惡劣的經濟環境下人們成功的可能性很小。
What are the odds on him being (= do you think he will be) re-elected?
他再次當選的幾率有多大？
The odds are stacked against a woman succeeding (= it is not likely that a woman will succeed) in the business.
女性在生意場上成功的可能性不大。
The odds against my horse winning (= that it will not win)/on my horse winning (= that it will win) are a hundred to one.
賭我的馬輸/贏的賠率是100比1。
The odds that the US entrant will win the race are ten to one.
賭美國選手在這次比賽中獲勝的賠率是10比1。

NONE: C2 various things of different types, usually small and not important, or of little value
零碎東西，零星雜物

example: I took most of the big things to the new house, but there are a few odds and ends left to pick up.
我把大部分大傢什都搬到新房去了，但還有些零碎的東西要收拾。

NONE: › very probable
很有可能的

example: The odds-on favourite to win in the 3.30 race is Killjoy.
3：30的賽馬中最被看好的獲勝者是「大煞星」。
UK It's odds-on she'll be late and I've rushed for no reason!
她很可能會遲到，我白白趕了一通！
